Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. blocks.text: Condo buildings in Bradner

Headline fact: Bradner has no condo stock — and by rule, it cannot stratify its farm residences. Bradner is a rural agricultural community partly in the Agricultural Land Reserve, and the Agricultural Land Commission's housing rules state that residences in the ALR cannot be stratified (cannot be converted into strata lots and sold separately).
Streets, schools and getting around Bradner

items.t: Municipality: City of Abbotsford, BC. Bradner is a rural, agricultural community on the west side of Abbotsford, partly in the Agricultural Land Reserve.
Bradner Road is the main road through the community and the corridor's search name; it leads south to Highway 1, and the City runs a dedicated engagement page for Bradner Road.

Nearby areas named in City material: McCallum Rural to the east, Aldergrove (Township of Langley) to the west, Matsqui Prairie to the south and Northeast Abbotsford to the northeast. Community landmarks are rural, not urban: Grant Park, a City sports park at 7399 Bradner Road, and Bradner Hall at 5305 Bradner Road.

Where condo stock concentrates: nowhere in Bradner. There is no town centre, transit node or multi-family corridor — no transit route summary for Bradner was found on the City's searched transit pages, and no grocery store inside Bradner was named on an official source.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Bradner

items.t: No stratification in the ALR: residences in the Agricultural Land Reserve cannot be stratified (converted into strata lots and sold separately) under the ALC housing rules.

ALR housing caps: one principal residence per parcel, maximum 500 m²; a secondary suite only inside the principal residence; an additional detached residence for farm use or another permitted use capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha. Agri-tourism and temporary farm worker housing are permitted under conditions.

SSMUH does not create Bradner condos: in June 2024 Council adopted Zoning Bylaw amendments implementing provincial small-scale multi-unit housing legislation. SSMUH targets lots previously limited to single-detached/duplex use; Bradner's agricultural A1/A2 zoning and the ALR no-stratification rule are the controlling framework here.

For a condo purchase in Abbotsford West/Central — Form B and depreciation reports: the strata must provide a Form B Information Certificate; since July 1, 2024 every strata with five or more lots must hold a depreciation report on a five-year cycle (30-year projection, at least three CRF funding models, no deferral vote), and since November 1, 2023 stratas must contribute at least 10% of the operating fund to the CRF annually.

Rentals and age (provincial): long-term rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 (Bill 44); short-term rentals can still be restricted. The only legal age bylaw is 55+ (Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2), with exemptions for legacy residents, live-in caregivers, and (from May 1, 2023) younger spouses/partners and defined children.

Taxes and rebates on a condo elsewhere in Abbotsford: BC PTT is 1% on the first $200,000, 2% to $2 million, 3% to $3 million, 5% above; first-time buyers pay no PTT on the first $500,000 at values of $835,000 or less (maximum saving $8,000, partial to $860,000) and the Newly Built Home Exemption is full to $1,100,000 (partial to $1,150,000). New condos carry 5% GST; the First-Time Home Buyers' GST/HST Rebate returns 100% of GST up to $1 million (maximum $50,000), phasing out to $1.5 million, for agreements on/after March 20, 2025; the older GST New Housing Rebate is 36%, maximum $6,300, $350,000–$450,000 phase-out.

Presales, savings vehicles, mortgage insurance (redirected buyers): REDMA s. 21 gives a 7-day presale rescission right and s. 18 requires deposits in trust; the Home Buyers' Plan allows $60,000 per buyer and the First Home Savings Account $40,000 lifetime / $8,000 per year; CMHC premiums run 0.60%–4.00% by loan-to-value (4.50% top band with a non-traditional down payment; +0.20% where the over-25-year surcharge applies).

blocks.text: Good to know about Bradner

items.t: The no-strata rule is the single most important "condo" fact about Bradner: because ALR residences cannot be stratified, there is no legal pathway for a Bradner farm property to become condo-style separately-sold homes — buyers pricing a parcel on a future strata exit are pricing something the ALC rules prohibit.

The catchment question for Bradner was genuinely unsettled until the locator run: district sources conflicted (the boundary-maps page named W.A. Fraser Middle for 5396 Bradner Road while Eugene Reimer's family-of-schools page named Reimer); the SD34 School Locator run on 2026-11-01 settled it as Eugene Reimer Middle, matching the feeder pattern Bradner Elementary → Eugene Reimer Middle → Rick Hansen Secondary.

A Bradner logging right-of-way is on the public record: retention of a Bradner logging right-of-way by A&A Trading Ltd. was confirmed in a City of Abbotsford council-agenda context (May 1, 2023 agenda) — a reminder that working-land rights, not development rights, are what change hands out here.

Property-tax timing is city-wide and applies to Bradner acreages: Abbotsford property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a first 5% penalty on July 3, 2026 and a second 5% penalty on September 16, 2026, each including any unclaimed Home Owner Grant.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Bradner
Zero verified townhouse stock: Bradner has no townhouse complex, strata or fee-simple, and by rule its ALR residences cannot be stratified without the Agricultural Land Commission's permission.
Streets, schools and getting around Bradner

items.t: Where townhouse stock concentrates: nowhere in Bradner. There is no town centre, transit node or multi-family corridor — no transit route summary for Bradner was found on the City's searched transit pages, and no grocery store inside Bradner was named on an official source.
SnapStats does not publish a townhome-only figure, and none is invented here.
Schools are address-based in SD34; for the test address 5396 Bradner Road the SD34 School Locator returns Bradner Elementary (K–5), Eugene Reimer Middle (6–8) and Rick Hansen Secondary (9–12).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Bradner

items.t: No stratification in the ALR without ALC permission: depositing a strata plan causes a subdivision (Strata Property Act s. 239), and agricultural land must not be subdivided unless permitted by the Commission or under the ALR General Regulation (ALCA s. 21(1); ALC Bulletin 09, s. 6). This is the single rule that decides the townhouse question in Bradner.

ALR housing caps: one principal residence per parcel, maximum 500 m² gross floor area, with no more than 1,000 m² of fill for its construction on the ALC's stated terms; a secondary suite only inside the principal residence; an additional detached residence for farm use or another permitted use capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha. Agri-tourism and temporary farm worker housing are permitted under conditions.

Farm-class thresholds — the full three tiers (a flat "$2,500+" line is an error and must never be published for Bradner): (1) $2,500 in farm income on parcels of 0.8–4 ha; (2) $2,500 plus 5% of the value of the area in excess of 4 ha on operations over 4 ha; (3) $10,000 in farm income on parcels under 0.8 ha; farm classification applications must be submitted by October 31 for the following taxation year.
City zoning and plan: Bradner lands are A1/A2 Agricultural under the City of Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014. The current city plan is Abbotsforward 2050 (adopted December 2025).

SSMUH does not create Bradner townhouses — the A1/A2 zoning and the ALR no-stratification rule are the controlling framework here, and on ALR land the suite must sit inside the principal residence in any case.

A Bradner house purchase has no strata, no Form B and no strata fees — municipal zoning, ALR rules, and any registered covenants on title govern. The strata block below applies only if the buyer redirects to a townhouse elsewhere in Abbotsford.

For a strata townhouse elsewhere in Abbotsford — Form B, depreciation reports, CRF: the strata must provide a Form B Information Certificate (Strata Property Act s. 59); since July 1, 2024 every strata with five or more lots must hold a depreciation report on a five-year cycle (a sub-5-lot strata sits UNDER that threshold), and since November 1, 2023 stratas must contribute at least 10% of the operating fund to the CRF annually.

Rentals and age (provincial): long-term rental-restriction bylaws are void since November 24, 2022. The only legal age bylaw is 55+ (Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2), with the May 1, 2023 expanded exemptions.

Tax timing: City of Abbotsford property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a first 5% penalty on July 3, 2026 and a second 5% penalty on September 16, 2026, each including any unclaimed Home Owner Grant.

GST and rebates: the FTHB GST rebate — Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026 per CRA News No. 122 — rebates 100% of GST to $1M (maximum $50,000), phasing to $1.5M, agreements March 20, 2025–2031; the New Housing Rebate is 36% / maximum $6,300 / $350K–$450K. PTT, compression flagged: 1% / 2% / 3% tiers plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3M — a page's "Over $3M — 5%" row compresses that 3% + 2%; first-time buyer exemption on the first $500,000 up to $835,000 (partial to $860,000), Newly Built Home Exemption full to $1,100,000 (partial to $1,150,000). HBP $60,000; FHSA $40,000 lifetime / $8,000 per year; CMHC premiums 0.6%–4.5%.
Presales (REDMA), redirected buyers only: s. 21 gives a 7-day rescission right and s. 18 requires deposits in trust — no Bradner presale exists for these to attach to.

blocks.text: Good to know about Bradner

items.t: The no-strata rule is the single most important "townhouse" fact about Bradner: because a strata plan is a subdivision of ALR land requiring ALC permission, there is no as-of-right pathway for a Bradner farm property to become separately-sold townhouse-style homes — buyers pricing a parcel on a future strata exit are pricing something the ALC rules do not grant.
Abbotsford's current plan is Abbotsforward 2050 (adopted December 2025) — growth directed at the urban nodes, while Bradner's framework remains A1/A2 agricultural zoning.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Bradner
What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple parcels are the only land form: A Bradner land purchase is a fee-simple title purchase: no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fee — City zoning, ALR rules where the parcel is in the reserve, and any registered covenants on title govern.
Lot character, stated with its limit: A parcel bought for its "future lots" is bought against those minimums.
ALR vs non-ALR split: The split is the whole diligence question here, because ALR status changes subdivision (ALC approval), housing (the ALC caps) and tenure (no stratification) at once.
Bare-land strata: none — and structurally barred on ALR ground: A bare-land strata lot, where the form lawfully exists elsewhere, is strata tenure — Form B, strata fees and bylaws apply to the lot.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Bradner

items.t: Where land actually trades: as whole fee-simple farm and rural-residential parcels along the Bradner Road corridor — there is no lot subdivision, no serviced-lot product and no development node in the community. No transit route summary for Bradner was found on the City's searched transit pages, and no grocery store inside Bradner was named on an official source.
SnapStats publishes no land category (Detached vs "Condos & Townhomes" combined only), so no figure here is presented as a land figure — the detached row simply shows the parcel market's pace.
Schools are address-based in SD34; the one settled locator chain for the community (5396 Bradner Road) is carried in — with its correction: the middle school is Eugene Reimer Middle, not W.A. Fraser.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Bradner

items.t: Zoning: A1 and A2 Agricultural under Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014: The city-wide A1/A2 subdivision minimums carried in the Abbotsford AgRefresh material are 8.0 ha (A1) and 16.0 ha (A2); the current zoning section for a specific parcel governs and should be read before those figures are relied on.

ALR rules — the governing frame for ALR parcels: subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval, stated as the ALC states it. ALR residences cannot be stratified — cannot be converted into strata lots and sold separately (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; Strata Property Act s.239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s.21(1)). Residence caps as the ALC states them: one principal residence per parcel, maximum gross floor area 500 m²; a secondary suite permitted only inside the principal residence; an additional residence (a second, detached, small-scale residence for farm use or other permitted use) capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha. Agri-tourism and temporary farm worker housing are permitted under conditions.

Farm class (BC Assessment) — the full three-tier form, never the flat figure: $2,500 of farm income on a farm operation of 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the farm operation for farm purposes in excess of 4 ha on operations over 4 ha; $10,000 on operations under 0.8 ha — Classification of Land as a Farm Regulation, B.C. Reg. 411/95, s.5, with applications by October 31. Farm class is the holding-cost difference between a working Bradner parcel and an idle one — confirm the parcel's current class and the income record before pricing the tax position.

SSMUH — present in Abbotsford, not a Bradner land lever: June 2024 Council adoption of Abbotsford's SSMUH Zoning Bylaw amendments is City-confirmed. Abbotsford's suite cap is under 50% of the principal dwelling and its coach/garden suite cap is 15% of lot area to a maximum of 100 m² (Abbotsford's rules only) — but on ALR land the ALC suite rule (inside the principal residence only) and the A1/A2 zoning are the controlling framework, and SSMUH creates no Bradner lots and no Bradner strata.

If a strata purchase is made elsewhere in Abbotsford (redirect case): the BC strata block applies — Form B diligence; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions). None of it applies to a Bradner fee-simple parcel purchase itself: no strata, no Form B, no strata fees.

GST on farm and vacant land — stated only at the level the CRA sources support: CRA Info Sheet GI-003 states most sales of vacant land by individuals are exempt (personal-use land is the example), while an individual's sale can be taxable where the land is capital property used primarily in a business, is sold in the course of a business, or is a subdivided parcel of more than two parts. Farmland is the caution: the CRA addresses sales of farmland by individuals in a SEPARATE info sheet and treats farmland sales as usually taxable subject to limited exemptions (including certain transfers to a related person for personal use). A Bradner farm purchase must therefore never be assumed GST-exempt on the "vacant land" rule alone.

blocks.text: Good to know about Bradner

items.t: The middle-school correction is already settled — and pages still get it wrong. A district boundary-maps page named W.A. Fraser Middle for 5396 Bradner Road; the completed SD34 locator run and Eugene Reimer Middle's own family-of-schools page agree the chain is Bradner Elementary → Eugene Reimer Middle → Rick Hansen Secondary. Any Bradner land marketing that names W.A. Fraser is using the superseded source.
Bradner's land frame was set by farm policy, not housing policy. The absence is the fact: this is working-land ground inside a city that is otherwise planning for growth.
The plan citation on rural Abbotsford pages is stale. The current plan still treats Bradner through its rural-village framework.
Zero attached listings is a structural zero, not a slow month. A buyer waiting for Bradner townhome or strata "lots" to come to market is waiting for a form the rules do not produce.

One hectare is 2.471 acres — the conversion every Bradner threshold needs. The ALC caps turn at 40 ha (≈98.8 acres) and the farm-class tiers at 0.8 ha and 4 ha; acreage listings that blur the conversion blur which cap and which income tier apply to the parcel.

blocks.text: Duplexes and half duplexes in Bradner
What a duplex looks like in Bradner

items.t: Why duplexes are limited here: Bradner lands are zoned A1 and A2 Agricultural under the City of Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw, and part of the area is in the ALR. On ALR land, residences cannot be stratified without the ALC's permission — depositing a strata plan is a subdivision (Strata Property Act s.239), and a person must not subdivide agricultural land unless permitted by the Commission or under the ALR General Regulation (Agricultural Land Commission Act s.21(1); ALC Information Bulletin 09, s.6).

The usual duplex form: Farm and rural-residential parcels and detached houses on agricultural land, effectively all fee-simple freehold under one title. On ALR land the ALC housing rules permit one principal residence per parcel (maximum 500 m² gross floor area), a secondary suite only inside the principal residence, and one additional detached residence for farm use or another permitted use — capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha. A principal home plus a lawful additional residence is a two-residence farm parcel, sold whole — it is not a duplex and neither residence is a separately titled half.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect duplexes in Bradner

items.t: Abbotsford's general rule: One secondary suite in single detached dwellings (s.140.3.8), sized at under 50% of the principal unit under the 2025 updates, with a coach/garden suite capped at 15% of the lot area to a maximum of 100 m² (Abbotsford only). On ALR land the ALC rule governs instead: A secondary suite is permitted only inside the principal residence — never in a barn or a detached building.

faq.q: Can I buy a condo in Bradner?

faq.a: No. Under the ALC housing rules, residences in the ALR cannot be stratified — they cannot be converted into strata lots and sold separately.
faq.q: Could a Bradner farm home be turned into condos later?

faq.a: One principal residence up to 500 m², a secondary suite inside that residence only, and one additional small residence for farm use or another permitted use — 90 m² maximum on parcels of 40 ha or less, 186 m² on larger parcels.
faq.q: What housing CAN be added on a Bradner farm parcel?

faq.a: No — a secondary suite is permitted only inside the principal residence; a detached second dwelling is the size-capped "additional residence" tied to farm use or another permitted use.
faq.q: Can a suite go in a barn or detached building?

faq.a: Partly — it is a rural agricultural community with lands zoned A1 and A2 Agricultural, part of it in the ALR; whether a specific parcel is in the ALR must be confirmed for that parcel.
faq.q: Is Bradner in the Agricultural Land Reserve?

faq.a: Not as of right. Depositing a strata plan is a subdivision of ALR land and cannot be done without the ALC's permission under ALCA s. 21(1).
faq.q: Could a Bradner farm home be turned into townhouses or condos later?

faq.a: One principal residence up to 500 m², a secondary suite inside that residence only, and one additional small residence for farm use or another permitted use — 90 m² maximum on parcels of 40 ha or less, 186 m² on larger parcels.
faq.q: What housing CAN be added on a Bradner farm parcel?

faq.a: A whole fee-simple farm or rural-residential parcel under A1 or A2 Agricultural zoning, part of the community in the ALR. There is no acreage subdivision, no bare-land strata and no presale acreage product to buy instead — and no parcel-size statistic is published for the area, so each parcel is judged on its own title, zoning and ALR status.
faq.q: What am I actually buying when I buy an "acreage" in Bradner?

faq.a: No — under the ALC housing rules a secondary suite is permitted only inside the principal residence. A detached second dwelling is the "additional residence," size-capped and tied to farm use or another permitted use. Abbotsford's general suite and coach/garden caps do not override the ALR rule on ALR land.
faq.q: Can a suite go in a barn or a detached building?

faq.a: Property taxes on the Abbotsford cycle (due July 2, 2026; 5% penalty July 3; second 5% September 16, 2026), with farm class — if the parcel qualifies and the income is actually produced and reported — as the main reducer. Add well/septic maintenance and any right-of-way or covenant obligations on title. There is no strata fee: the parcel is fee-simple.
faq.q: What will it cost to hold the acreage?

faq.a: No. That wording is a record of marketing language for a two-unit or two-residence farm property; without a strata plan or a subdivided lot there is no separate half to buy.
faq.q: A listing calls a Bradner farmhouse a duplex — can I buy one side?

faq.a: Bradner Elementary, at 5291 Bradner Road, is the in-community school. The district describes it as a community school whose roots reach back into the late 1800s, with many past pupils still living and working in the area. Catchments are address-based in District 34, so confirm the property address
faq.q: Which elementary school is in Bradner itself?

faq.a: District 34 catchments are address-based, so run the specific address through the district locator
faq.q: Where do Bradner students go after elementary school?

faq.a: No. The City profiles Bradner with Mt. Lehman as small historic rural centres surrounded by agricultural lands in the northwest corner. That is why agricultural zoning and Agricultural Land Reserve rules, not urban infill rules, frame most buying questions here
faq.q: Is Bradner part of urban Abbotsford?

faq.a: Bradner Hall, at 5305 Bradner Road, is the community hall: the City used it for a Bradner agriculture open house, and the City profile names it as the hall where the annual Bradner Daffodil Show is held, beside the elementary school
faq.q: What is Bradner Hall used for?
